arxiv-2101-12653.title: Non-adaptive Combinatorial Quantitative Group Testing with Adversarially Perturbed Measurements
arxiv-2101-12653.creator: Yun-Han Li, I-Hsiang Wang
arxiv-2101-12653.description: Abstract In this paper, combinatorial quantitative group testing (QGT) with noisy measurements is studied. The goal of QGT is to detect defective items from a data set of size n n with counting measurements, each of which counts the number of defects in a selected pool of items.

arxiv-2208-09031.description: Abstract A foundational idea in the theory of in situ planet formation is the “minimum mass extrasolar nebula” (MMEN), a surface density profile ( Σ \Sigma ) of disk solids that is necessary to form the planets in their present locations.

arxiv-2209-10906.title: Spin wave study of magnetic perpendicular surface anisotropy in single crystalline MgO / Fe / MgO films
arxiv-2209-10906.creator: J. Solano, O. Gladii, P. Kuntz, Y. Henry, D. Halley, M. Bailleul
arxiv-2209-10906.description: Abstract Broadband ferromagnetic resonance is measured in single crystalline Fe films of varying thickness sandwiched between MgO layers. An exhaustive magnetic characterization of the films (exchange constant, cubic, uniaxial and surface anisotropies) is enabled by the study of the uniform and the first perpendicular standing spin wave modes as a function of applied magnetic field and film thickness.

arxiv-2309-01570.title: Advancing the lower bounds: An accelerated, stochastic, second-order method with optimal adaptation to inexactness
arxiv-2309-01570.creator: Artem Agafonov, Dmitry Kamzolov, Alexander Gasnikov, Ali Kavis, Kimon Antonakopoulos, Volkan Cevher, Martin Takáč
arxiv-2309-01570.description: Abstract We present a new accelerated stochastic second-order method that is robust to both gradient and Hessian inexactness, which occurs typically in machine learning. We establish theoretical lower bounds and prove that our algorithm achieves optimal convergence in both gradient and Hessian inexactness in this key setting. We further introduce a tensor generalization for stochastic higher-order derivatives.

arxiv-2310-11115.title: Heat kernel fluctuations and quantitative homogenization for the one-dimensional Bouchaud trap model
arxiv-2310-11115.creator: Sebastian Andres, David A. Croydon, Takashi Kumagai
arxiv-2310-11115.description: Abstract . We present on-diagonal heat kernel estimates and quantitative homogenization statements for the one-dimensional Bouchaud trap model. The heat kernel estimates are obtained using standard techniques, with key inputs coming from a careful analysis of the volume growth of the invariant measure of the process under study.

arxiv-2311-17893.title: Betrayed by Attention: A Simple yet Effective Approach for Self-supervised Video Object Segmentation
arxiv-2311-17893.creator: Shuangrui Ding, Rui Qian, Haohang Xu, Dahua Lin, Hongkai Xiong
arxiv-2311-17893.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective approach for self-supervised video object segmentation (VOS). Previous self-supervised VOS techniques majorly resort to auxiliary modalities or utilize iterative slot attention to assist in object discovery, which restricts their general applicability.

arxiv-2312-11801.title: Fast, Scalable, Warm-Start Semidefinite Programming with Spectral Bundling and Sketching
arxiv-2312-11801.creator: Rico Angell, Andrew McCallum
arxiv-2312-11801.description: Abstract While semidefinite programming (SDP) has traditionally been limited to moderate-sized problems, recent algorithms augmented with matrix sketching techniques have enabled solving larger SDPs. However, these methods achieve scalability at the cost of an increase in the number of necessary iterations, resulting in slower convergence as the problem size grows.

arxiv-2401-01403.creator: Megan Masterson, Kishalay De, Christos Panagiotou, Erin Kara, Iair Arcavi, Anna-Christina Eilers, Danielle Frostig, Suvi Gezari, Iuliia Grotova, Zhu Liu, Adam Malyali, Aaron M. Meisner, Andrea Merloni, Megan Newsome, Arne Rau, Robert A. Simcoe, Sjoert van Velzen
arxiv-2401-01403.description: Abstract Most tidal disruption events (TDEs) are currently found in time-domain optical and soft X-ray surveys, both of which are prone to significant obscuration. The infrared (IR), however, is a powerful probe of dust-enshrouded environments, and hence, we recently performed a systematic search of NEOWISE mid-IR data for nearby, obscured TDEs within roughly 200 Mpc.

arxiv-2403-08558.title: Narrowly-Banded Spectra with Peak Frequency Around 1 GHz of FRB 20201124A: Implications for Energy Function and Radiation Physics
arxiv-2403-08558.creator: Fen Lyu, En-Wei Liang*, D. Li*
arxiv-2403-08558.description: Abstract The radiation physics of fast radio bursts (FRBs) remains an open question. Current observations have discovered that narrowly-banded bursts of FRB 20201124A are active in 0.4-2 GHz and their spectral peak frequency ( ν p obs \nu^{\rm obs}_{p} ) are mostly toward ∼ 1 \sim 1 GHz.

pmc-13468484.title: Development and Challenges of Food Contaminant Removal Technologies: Molecular Imprinting Technology as an Emerging Solution

pmc-13468484.description: Food contaminants, including plasticizers, pesticide residues, heavy metals, and biotoxins, pose persistent risks to food quality and human health.
